claims.text: UN News (citing OHCHR/UN High Commissioner Volker Turk), reporting on Yemen: 'at least 17 civilians were killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas since August 6, 2026.' Specific incidents cited: a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Ma'rib (7 August) injuring six civilians including a child; missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port in Ta'izz Governorate (9 August) killing three port workers and injuring four others; and an attack on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (11 August) killing four crew members (three Pakistani nationals, one Indonesian) with additional injuries. Turk said: 'I call on all parties to de-escalate tensions and spare the Yemeni people from further misery' and 'These attacks must end immediately.'

UN News, Security Council coverage (13 August 2026): UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg briefed the Security Council warning Yemen 'faces a more serious risk of return to large-scale conflict than at any point since' the 2022 UN-mediated truce, citing intensifying military activity along the frontline and pressure on regional trade and energy flows. UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher told the Council more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity, and with the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded, 'rations are cut, clinics close and protection services disappear'; both officials called for the immediate release of 73 UN colleagues still arbitrarily detained by the Houthis.

description: Yemen's conflict escalated sharply from early August 2026 as Houthi (Ansar Allah) missile and drone attacks on government-held areas and on shipping intensified. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk reported at least 17 civilians killed in attacks on government-controlled areas since 6 August 2026, citing a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Ma'rib (7 August) that injured six civilians including a child, missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port in Ta'izz Governorate (9 August) that killed three port workers, and an attack on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (11 August) that killed four crew members. Briefing the Security Council on 13 August, UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg warned Yemen faces a more serious risk of return to large-scale conflict than at any point since the 2022 UN-mediated truce, citing intensifying frontline military activity and pressure on regional trade and energy flows. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity with the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded; both officials called for the immediate release of 73 detained UN colleagues.

impact.summary: At least 17 civilians have been killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas of Yemen since 6 August 2026, per UN High Commissioner Volker Turk -- including three port workers killed at Al-Mokha port (9 August) and four crew members killed on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (11 August). UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council on 13 August that Yemen faces a more serious risk of return to large-scale conflict than at any point since the 2022 truce, with more than half the population facing acute food insecurity and the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded. No aggregate displacement figure specific to this escalation has been published.

location.region: Ma'rib and Al-Mokha (Ta'izz Governorate); attacks also in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait

event.scale: At least 17 civilians killed since 6 Aug 2026; UN warns of highest risk of full-scale war since 2022 truce
